source: described (Cal.com / Notion Calendar / Linear — dense, readable interface conventions, no screenshots measured)

neutral.usage: text/ink from #17140F (near-black, warm — matches logo black) down to #8A8478 for tertiary/meta text; never pure #000 or pure #FFF to keep the warm, non-generic feel

primary.usage: the one accent — active states, primary actions, occupancy fill, selected day/PT

accent.usage: dark for pressed/hover, light for subtle tints (chips, selected-cell backgrounds), tint_10 for faint fills — gold never used as large background fields, only as accents/states

semantic.usage: status colors kept separate from brand gold so 'full slot' vs 'selected/active' are never visually confused

typography.family_display: condensed/bold geometric sans for headings and numerals (e.g. Barlow Condensed / Archivo — echoes the logo's bold blocky wordmark)
typography.family_body: humanist sans, high x-height, strong at small sizes (e.g. Inter / Manrope)
typography.family_mono: for time labels/durations only if needed (e.g. JetBrains Mono) — optional, not required
typography.notes: Cal.com/Linear keep body text small (13-15px) but high-contrast and tightly leaded in dense views (calendar, tables); headings jump in weight not just size.

spacing.density: high but breathable — 8-12px internal padding in list rows/cells, 16-24px between logical groups, no dead air
spacing.rhythm: consistent 8px grid; section gaps are a multiple of 24px, never arbitrary

layout.grid: 12-col on desktop with a fixed-width time axis for calendar; single-column stacked on mobile
layout.max_width: desktop shell max ~1440px, calendar grid fills remaining space
layout.asymmetry: sidebar/filters + wide content, not centered marketing-style layouts

shape.border_usage: 1px hairline borders (#E4E0D6) preferred over shadows to separate cells/rows — this is the key Cal.com/Linear trick for dense UI: structure via lines, not elevation

elevation.philosophy: near-flat; shadow reserved for genuinely floating layers (bottom sheet, dropdown, modal) — never on static cards

motion.easing: ease-out for entrances, ease-in-out for state toggles
motion.notes: motion is reactive only — triggered by user action (tap, toggle, drag), never ambient/decorative

design_style.mood: confident, calm, professional — 'well-run facility' not 'flashy startup'
design_style.composition_strategy: information hierarchy via type weight + spacing + one accent color, not via decoration
design_style.ornamentation: minimal to none — no gradients, no dual shadows, no decorative icons without function
design_style.whitespace_philosophy: generous between sections, tight within data (rows/cells) — density is earned by grouping, not by cramming everything uniformly

visual_effects.notes: not applicable — this is a functional dashboard; motion only, no canvas/WebGL/particle effects

principles_summary: Structure with hairline borders, not shadows — shadows only for floating layers (sheets/menus/dropdowns)
One accent color used sparingly and consistently (state + action), never as a background field
Status/occupancy communicated via color + icon/shape together, never color alone
Type does the hierarchy work: weight and size jumps, not boxes and gradients
Dense views stay legible via consistent 8px rhythm and a fixed reference axis (time column) the eye can anchor to
Motion responds to touch/interaction only — no idle animation, no scroll-triggered spectacle
